top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, verified invention: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the clock-transition light shift while holding many neutral atoms in a Lamb-Dicke lattice, which neither the 2005 comb prize nor the 2012 single-quantum-system prize contains. Independent laboratories and species agree at the 1e-18 level, so maturity is established without waiting for the redefinition of the second. Katori (proposal and first Sr lattice clock) and Ye (record accuracy, stability and many-body clock physics) are separable, decisive contributions, and a two-name award with an 'invention and realization' citation keeps the attribution clean. The topological-insulator trio (P002) ranks second as a mature, falsifiable concept with an incomplete credit chain, and the twisted-bilayer-graphene proposal (P003) is younger, with the superconductivity mechanism and sample dependence unsettled, but I still prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: Possible Chalmers/WACQT proximity to optical-clock or quantum-technology colleagues is not documented; none apparent from profile for these proposals (B046, B038, B042). Professional links to Delsing, Wilson and Kockum concern superconducting circuits, which are not on the slate.
